title: Almoravid Dynasty
capsule: The Almoravid dynasty (al-Murābiṭūn) originated among the Sanhaja Berber confederation of the western Sahara, where the reformer Abdallah ibn Yasin forged a militant Islamic movement in the 1040s. Under Yusuf ibn Tashfin (r. 1061–1106), the dynasty conquered Morocco and founded Marrakesh (1062), crossed into al-Andalus in 1086 to defeat Alfonso VI of Castile at the Battle of Sagrajas, and unified Muslim Iberia under North African rule. Almoravid authority in Iberia collapsed under Almohad pressure in the mid-twelfth century, and the Almohads completed their overthrow of the Almoravids in Morocco by 1147, though Almoravid successor states persisted in the Balearic Islands until 1203.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Moroccan and Andalusian heartlands are well attested; Saharan frontier zones and the precise extent of Almoravid influence south of the Senegal River are reconstructed from partial chronicles and archaeological evidence.
